steps.title: Prepare compound source plates
steps.instruction: Dissolve each test and reference compound in DMSO to a 1000‑fold higher concentration than the intended assay concentration (1 µM → 1 mM, 10 µM → 10 mM) so that the final DMSO concentration in the assay is ≤0.1 % (v/v). Add at least 3 µL of each 1000× stock to a well of a 384‑well LDV source plate (Labcyte), centrifuge the plate at 500 × g for 3 min, seal with VWR DMSO‑resistant seals, and store at –20 °C (up to 2 years). Before reuse, thaw the plate at room temperature for ≥1 h, inspect for precipitation, verify sufficient volume with the Echo 550 survey detection function, and use polypropylene plates to minimise wall absorption.

steps.title: Prepare reference compounds
steps.instruction: Dissolve staurosporine, paclitaxel, milciclib, daunorubicin, digitonin and berzosertib in DMSO to 10 mM (final assay concentration 10 µM). Add a minimum of 3 µL of each reference compound to an individual well of the LDV source plate.

steps.title: Create Echo 550 pick list
steps.instruction: Use the Echo 550 “Pick list” program (Agilent manual) to generate a CSV file that transfers the desired nanoliter volumes from source to destination plate. Include all test compounds, reference compounds (in technical quadruplicate), and DMSO blank wells (5–10 % of plate). Save the list as “.csv”.

substeps.instruction: Define source plate name, source well, destination plate name, destination well, and transfer volume (nL).
Example entries: 250 nL from Source A01 → Destination B02 for Compound 1, 50 nL DMSO for blank wells.

steps.title: Dispense compounds to assay plate
steps.instruction: Using the Echo 550 and the prepared pick list, transfer compounds into a 384‑well assay plate so that each well contains 50 µL total volume. For 10 µM test wells transfer 50 nL of 10 mM stock (or 5 nL of 1 mM stock for 1 µM wells); the remaining ~45 nL DMSO is negligible, keeping final DMSO at 0.1 % (v/v). Add reference compounds in technical quadruplicate, test compounds in technical duplicate, and DMSO blanks (50 nL DMSO per well).

substeps.instruction: Verify that the Echo reports successful dispensing for each well.
Avoid compounds with limited DMSO solubility; if precipitation occurs, re‑dissolve in water and dispense manually or with the Echo aqueous protocol (384LDV_aq).

steps.title: Set CQ1 imaging parameters
steps.instruction: Program the Yokogawa CQ1 microscope with the following settings: 10× objective (alternatives: 20× for higher detail, 2× not recommended); five fluorescence channels – Ex 405 nm/Em 447/60 nm (500 ms, 50 %); Ex 561 nm/Em 617/73 nm (100 ms, 40 %); Ex 488 nm/Em 525/50 nm (50 ms, 40 %); Ex 640 nm/Em 685/40 nm (50 ms, 20 %); brightfield (300 ms, 100 % transmission). Acquire 7 Z‑stacks spanning a total of 55 µm (e.g., bottom –20.2 µm, top +39.7 µm) with a focus height of 14.4 ± 0.1 mm and a focus offset of –15.5 µm. Use the same plate type in the CQ1 software as in the assay.

steps.title: Install Python analysis environment
steps.instruction: Download and install Anaconda (Python 3) from https://www.anaconda.com, follow the Getting Started guide, and note the displayed root path (to be used later). Then create the analysis environment by following the instructions on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6325622) and record the exact software version (e.g., v1.0.1, DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6327204).

steps.title: Load CellPathfinder protocol
steps.instruction: Open CellPathfinder (Yokogawa), click the “Data” tab, browse to the folder containing the CQ1 measurement files and press “Convert”. In the “Protocol” tab load the pre‑made analysis protocol for U‑2 OS multiplex (CellPathfinder_AnalysisProtocol_U2OS_Multiplex) from Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6415330).

steps.title: Configure channels and objects
steps.instruction: In the “Channels” section define six channels: CH1 – Hoechst 33342 (Ex 405/Em 447/60); CH2 – BioTracker 488 Green Microtubule Dye (Ex 488/Em 525/50); CH3 – MitoTracker Red (Ex 561/Em 617/73); CH4 – Annexin V (Ex 640/Em 685/40); CH5 – brightfield DCP Fluor Type Simple Mode (Contrast 0.06); CH6 – brightfield DCP Phase Type Simple Mode (Contrast 0.04). For CH5 and CH6 select two Z‑stacks (Top Z5 and Bottom Z3) to overlay for optimal digital phase contrast. In the “Object” section create two objects: “Nucleus” (Ex 405/Em 447/60, Finder Nuclear, Recognition Advance) and “Cell body” (brightfield, Finder Cell, Recognition Advance). Link each nucleus to one cell body (1:1).

steps.title: Pre‑analyze reference wells
steps.instruction: Select wells containing the reference compounds (e.g., N5‑N12 and O5‑O12) and click “Pre‑Analyze” to generate object detection for nuclei and cell bodies. Verify correct detection in 5–10 example wells.

steps.title: Train machine‑learning gating
steps.instruction: Using the reference‑compound wells, train the ML‑based gating tree: (1) Separate Hoechst High‑Intensity Objects (“HighIntObj”) from “Normal” cells; (2) Split “Normal” into HealthyNuc, PyknoNuc, FragNuc; (3) Split PyknoNuc into “mitosis” or “apoptosis”; (4) From HealthyNuc branch further gate into tubulin effect/normal, mito mass high/normal, and membrane permeabilized/intact. For each gating node select at least 10 representative images (provided or chosen by a trained scientist).

substeps.instruction: Consult Table S2 on Zenodo for the full feature list.
After training, run the analysis on all reference‑compound wells and confirm that the phenotype frequencies differ by ≤10 % from expected values.

steps.title: Run full‑plate analysis and export data
steps.instruction: If the reference‑well validation passes, execute the trained protocol on the entire 384‑well plate (all time points). Upon completion, locate the output CSV files in the “…\PFAnalysis” subfolder and proceed to downstream data evaluation.

description: Here, we describe a high content multiplex screen, able to characterize generic effects regarding basic cell properties and cell viability in a multi-dimensional way, using phenotypic characterization to annotate compounds on their suitability for further phenotypic and mechanistic screening. The present protocol describes the workflow for 135 test compounds, screened at two concentrations (1 and 10 μM) in addition to 6 control compounds in a single 384 well plate, measured for a total of 48 h at 4 different time points. The protocol below describes the specific steps for testing osteosarcoma cells (U-2 OS). However, we have adapted this protocol to other cell lines including human embryonic kidney cells (HEK293T) and human fibroblasts (MRC-9) (see problem 1).
